Subject: DPA clarifications: controller/processor roles, subprocessors, breach notice

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the time earlier today — really appreciate the productive discussion and the context on Acme Payments' data flows. Per our call I wanted to follow up with a concise recap of the privacy items you raised and next steps: 

- Controller vs processor: you asked us to confirm whether Redwood is acting as a processor for Acme (i.e., processing customer data on your behalf) and whether that is reflected in our standard DPA.
- Subprocessors: you asked for the current subprocessors list and whether we provide advance notice of changes.
- Breach notice / incident response: you requested timing guarantees for notification of breaches impacting customer data.
- Data residency & retention: clarifying options for hosting EU data and default retention windows for request/trace logs.

I've attached our current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) and the SOC2 report for context. Rishi (legal) and Vivek are looped for any contract/legal clarifications.

Proposed next steps:
1) Rishi to confirm controller/processor language and subprocessors + notification process.
2) We can share a hosted-region/residency note (short doc) and retention defaults.
3) If it helps, we can schedule a follow-up 30m call with Rishi and your security contact to walk through the DPA line-by-line.

Does that work on your side? If so, any preference for Tuesday morning your time (US EDT)?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications: controller/processor roles, subprocessors, breach notice

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the documents. A few quick clarifying Qs from our side after a quick read-through: 

1) Controller/Processor: Our legal team wants an explicit statement in the DPA that Acme Payments is the Controller and Redwood acts as a Processor for customer-provided data used in inference. Can you confirm that is standard and can be reflected in the executed DPA?

2) Subprocessors: Please provide the current list of subprocessors (vendors, analytics, cloud infra partners) and confirm whether Redwood provides 30 days notice of any新增 subprocessors or if you permit customer objections.

3) Breach notice: We need a contractual commitment for notification timing (our policy asks for notification within 48 hours of detection for incidents affecting customer data). Is Redwood able to commit to 48 hours or do you operate with a 72-hour SLA? Also please outline what data you will provide in the initial notification.

4) Data residency & retention: For PCI-adjacent workloads we need EU residency and a retention policy for request/trace logs (preferably not kept longer than 90 days without explicit consent). What's Redwood's default and can this be configured per-account?

We may also need to share a short security questionnaire (I can send it) after legal looks over your SOC2.

Thanks — can we aim to lock these items before we move to procurement?

Best,
Samir
Director, Engineering
Acme Payments

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@acmepayments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.s@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications: controller/processor roles, subprocessors, breach notice

Hi Samir —

Appreciate the detailed questions. Below are concise answers from legal/ops that we can incorporate into the DPA or an addendum: 

1) Controller/Processor: Redwood's standard position is that the customer (Acme Payments) is the Controller; Redwood acts as a Processor when processing customer-provided data for inference and embeddings. We can add an explicit clause to the DPA reflecting this relationship and the corresponding obligations.

2) Subprocessors: We maintain a published list of subprocessors (cloud infra providers, metrics/monitoring, logging vendors). Current list includes: AWS (EC2/EKS/S3), Google Cloud (BigQuery where used for analytics), Datadog (monitoring), and an HSM/KMS partner for key management. We provide advance notice of material changes to subprocessors and a 30-day notice window for additions. Customers can object and request reasonable mitigations; for deal-specific carve-outs we can discuss contract language.

3) Breach notice / incident response: Our standard notification practice is to provide initial notification within 72 hours of confirmed detection for incidents impacting customer data. For high-priority incidents we often notify earlier. We can discuss whether 48 hours is required for Acme and any trade-offs (e.g., additional contractual SLAs and financial exposure). Initial notification will include: summary of impacted systems, scope of data types (PII categories, whether full request payloads were involved), mitigation steps underway, and contact points for follow-up.

4) Data residency & retention: Hosted API is multi-region by default but we offer options: (a) Hosted US/EU region pinning for account data, (b) Redwood Dedicated with capacity in a region you select, or (c) Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for strict residency. Default request/trace log retention is 30 days; this can be extended or shortened via contractual terms (we've accommodated 90-day limits in prior agreements).

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa: confirm Acme's preferred breach-notice SLA (48h vs 72h) so legal can scope contract language.
- Vivek/Hannah: prepare a short residency note describing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options and any pricing/ops implications.
- I'll prepare DPA language updates (controller/processor clause + subprocessors notice) and share redlines for Acme to review.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week to walk the DPA with your legal/security team.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SOC2_report_2025.pdf

Subject: Re: DPA clarifications: controller/processor roles, subprocessors, breach notice

Thanks Rishi — that is helpful and mostly aligns with what we expected. A few quick items on our side: 

- Controller/Processor clause: we can accept Redwood as Processor as long as the executed DPA contains the explicit language. Please include this in the redline.
- Subprocessors: please send the published subprocessors URL and, if possible, a static list for the next 30 days so our procurement team can review.
- Breach notice: Acme's standard is 48 hours for initial notification; if Redwood cannot contractually commit to 48 hours, confirm whether you can provide an operational escalation and what earlier notification cadence looks like (e.g., immediate 'we are investigating' message + fuller update within 72 hours).
- Docs we need to proceed: signed DPA (DocuSign), SOC2 report, and a PO for procurement. I've attached our PO (Acme_PO_5678.pdf).

If you can share the DocuSign link for the DPA and a short residency note (Hosted vs Dedicated options) by EOD Tuesday, procurement will move forward. Also happy to take the 30m call this week if helpful.

Best,
Lina Ortiz
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Payments
